title: Command and Mediator
idea: Command turns a request into an object you can store, queue or undo. Mediator puts one object between peers so they talk through it, not to each other.
points: A command object holds the receiver and arguments, plus `run` and `undo`.
The invoker keeps executed commands on a stack, so undo pops the last.
A mediator owns the rules for how a group of peers coordinates.
Peers hold one reference, the mediator, instead of references to every peer.

steps.caption: The first request becomes an object. `exec` calls its `run`, which edits `doc`.
After running, the command is pushed onto the history stack.
The second command runs the same way. `Editor` never knows what `Append` does inside.
It lands on top of the stack, above the first one.
Both commands have changed the document.
`undo` pops the top command and calls its own `undo`. Only the last change is reversed.

code.caption: The code from the animation. Add a second `ed.undo()` and predict the text first.

walk.text: The receiver: the object the command acts on.
`Append` stores its receiver and argument, and saves the old text so it can reverse itself.
The invoker runs any command and records it.
`?.` makes undo on an empty history a safe no-op.
Requests are objects, so they can be stored, queued or replayed.
Undo reverses only the most recent command.

code.title: Mediator: control tower
code.caption: Planes never reference each other. Add a third plane; no `Plane` code changes.

walk.text: `Tower` is the mediator. It keeps the peers and the shared runway state.
Joining gives each plane one link: back to the tower.
The landing rule lives here: clear one plane, tell the others.
A `Plane` only asks the tower and listens for notices.
The second plane is told to hold; it never asked `A1` directly.

pitfalls: Store enough state in each command to undo it; read the receiver before changing it.
Split a mediator that absorbs every rule; it becomes a god object.
Skip Command for plain calls that never need queuing, logging or undo.

quiz.why: Both commands run, making 8. `pop` removes the last command, the one that added 3, and its `undo` subtracts 3.

takeaway: Command makes actions into objects; Mediator routes peer talk through one hub.
